source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"A complete loss of consciousness during exercise, which is not what heat cramps alone typically involve, contrary to the coach's concern","B":"Identical severity and presentation to heat stroke, similar to what the coach is currently assuming about this client's cramping","C":"Altered mental status with a very high core temperature, which describes heat stroke rather than the milder heat cramps this client may actually be experiencing","D":"Painful muscle spasms without altered mental status or hyperthermia, rather than the impending heat stroke the coach is currently worried this represents"}}
source_row.rationale: Heat cramps are generally characterized by painful muscle spasms, typically affecting the legs or abdominal muscles, occurring during or after vigorous exercise in hot conditions, usually without significant alteration in mental status or a dangerously elevated core body temperature — a milder heat-related illness compared to heat exhaustion (which includes more systemic symptoms like weakness and heavy sweating) or heat stroke (which involves altered mental status and marked hyperthermia).
source_row.source_detail: Distinguishing Heat Cramps from More Severe Heat Illness
source_row.source_name: CDC / American College of Sports Medicine — Heat-Related Illness Spectrum
